Are you an upcoming or recent graduate with a background in computer science, engineering, technology or another related technical field and an interest in product management?

The Disney Associate Product Manager Program 2027 offers an opportunity to begin a career in product management within Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology, one of the technology organisations responsible for developing and supporting products and platforms across Disney’s global media business.

The programme is structured as a two-year career accelerator designed to develop early-career product management talent through practical experience, formal training, mentorship, networking and exposure to different product teams.

Full-time hires for the programme will begin as a cohort in Summer 2027. Participants will also complete a team rotation at the 12-month mark, giving them exposure to multiple teams and product domains.

The position is currently listed for Glendale, California, and New York, New York, with the primary location identified as the Greater Los Angeles area. The final location and team placement will depend on business needs and team alignment at the time an offer is made.

The role was posted by Disney on September 15, 2026, under Job ID 10160554.

About the Disney Associate Product Manager Program

The Associate Product Manager, or APM, Program is intended to provide a structured entry point into product management for talented early-career professionals.

Rather than simply placing a new graduate into an entry-level position without structured development, Disney describes the programme as a two-year career accelerator.

The programme combines:

  • Full-time employment.
  • Hands-on product development experience.
  • Structured product management training.
  • Mentorship from Disney product leaders.
  • Cross-functional collaboration.
  • Data and user research.
  • Strategic problem-solving.
  • Leadership development.
  • Professional networking.
  • Exposure to multiple product teams through a rotation.

New hires will join the programme as a cohort in Summer 2027. After the first 12 months, participants will rotate to another team, allowing them to experience different product domains and broaden their understanding of product management.

This structure is particularly relevant to graduates who want to develop a career that combines technology, business strategy, user experience, data analysis and product development.

About Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology

The Associate Product Manager Program sits within Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology.

This is a global organisation made up of professionals working across areas such as:

  • Engineering.
  • Product development.
  • Design.
  • Technology.
  • Data science.
  • Product management.
  • Digital platforms.
  • Media technology.

The organisation’s work supports Disney’s media businesses and its portfolio of brands and platforms.

According to the job description, teams collaborate across brands including:

  • Disney+
  • Hulu
  • ESPN
  • ABC
  • ABC News
  • National Geographic
  • Marvel
  • Star Wars

The broader purpose is to combine technology and creativity to build products, improve consumer experiences and develop the technological infrastructure supporting Disney’s media business around the world.

For an aspiring product manager, this means the programme offers exposure to an environment where technology and entertainment intersect.

What Makes the Disney APM Program Different?

The role is designed around development rather than simply assigning graduates routine tasks.

The programme gives participants an opportunity to learn how products are conceived, developed, launched and improved.

Disney highlights three broad aspects of its technology and product environment:

Building the Future of Media

Disney’s technology teams work on platforms that support media, advertising and distribution.

This means product professionals can work on technology that contributes to how audiences discover, access and interact with content.

Reach, Scale and Impact

The products developed by Disney’s technology organisation support interactions with millions of consumers around the world.

For an APM, this provides the possibility of learning how product decisions operate at significant scale.

Innovation

Disney’s technology teams work on new products and platforms and address complex technical and business challenges.

The APM programme therefore provides exposure to product development in a large global media and entertainment organisation.

Two-Year Career Accelerator Structure

One of the central features of the opportunity is its two-year structure.

Year One: Building Product Management Foundations

During the initial stage, participants will develop practical experience working with product teams.

They can expect exposure to areas such as:

  • Product discovery.
  • Product requirements.
  • User stories.
  • Market research.
  • Data analysis.
  • Product strategy.
  • Roadmap development.
  • Feature development.
  • Launch planning.
  • Cross-functional collaboration.

The programme also provides structured training and mentorship.

Year Two: Team Rotation and Broader Product Exposure

At the 12-month mark, participants will rotate teams.

The purpose of the rotation is to provide exposure to multiple teams and product domains.

This can help participants develop a broader understanding of:

  • Different types of products.
  • Different customer or user needs.
  • Different technical environments.
  • Different business objectives.
  • Different product development approaches.
  • Cross-functional team structures.

The rotation is an important part of the programme because product management can vary considerably depending on the product, customers, technology and business model.

What Will an Associate Product Manager Do?

The role is formally positioned as Product Manager I (APM).

The successful candidate will assist with the development and execution of product strategies designed to support business objectives.

The role involves working throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and research through development and launch.

The position provides opportunities to learn from experienced product professionals while contributing to projects within The Walt Disney Company.

Key Responsibilities

The APM will work across several aspects of product management.

1. Collaborate With Product, Design and Engineering Teams

The APM will work with:

  • Product Managers.
  • Designers.
  • Engineers.
  • Other cross-functional stakeholders.

The objective is to help develop features within an assigned product domain.

This requires the ability to communicate effectively with people who have different professional backgrounds and responsibilities.

2. Develop Product Strategy

Participants will learn how to develop and communicate a strategic vision.

This includes thinking about:

  • User needs.
  • Business objectives.
  • Market trends.
  • Product opportunities.
  • Fan engagement.
  • Product improvements.

The role therefore goes beyond simply managing a list of technical tasks.

3. Write Product Requirements

The APM will write detailed product documentation.

This can include:

  • Product requirements.
  • User stories.
  • Feature documentation.
  • Strategy documents.
  • Other materials used to guide development.

Strong writing and communication skills are therefore important.

4. Work on OKRs and Product Roadmaps

The APM will work with leadership on:

  • Product strategy.
  • Objectives and Key Results.
  • Product roadmaps.

This introduces participants to the strategic planning side of product management.

5. Conduct Market and Competitor Research

Product managers need to understand the environment in which their products operate.

The APM will support product research by analysing competitor offerings.

This can help the product team understand:

  • What competing products offer.
  • How user experiences compare.
  • Where opportunities for improvement exist.
  • How market trends may affect product decisions.

6. Analyse Data

The role includes basic data analysis to inform product decisions.

Examples include analysing:

  • Usage metrics.
  • User behaviour.
  • Product performance.
  • Other relevant data.

The objective is to use evidence to understand problems and support product decisions.

7. Support Product Launches

The APM will contribute to feature launches and internal communications.

This provides experience with the transition from product development to implementation and release.

Skills Disney Is Looking For

The job posting identifies several basic qualifications.

Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills

Applicants should have strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

The ability to use data-driven insights to inform decisions and measure performance is particularly important.

A strong candidate should therefore be comfortable asking:

  • What problem are we solving?
  • What does the available data tell us?
  • How are users behaving?
  • What should we improve?
  • How can we measure whether an improvement worked?

Communication Skills

Excellent written and verbal communication skills are required.

Product managers frequently serve as a bridge between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

They need to communicate:

  • Product requirements.
  • Strategy.
  • User needs.
  • Business objectives.
  • Product decisions.
  • Roadmaps.
  • Priorities.

Product or Technical Experience

Disney does not require applicants to have already worked as professional product managers.

The posting accepts experience gained through:

  • Coursework.
  • Academic projects.
  • Internships.

Relevant areas include:

  • Product management.
  • Engineering.
  • Software development.
  • User experience.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to students and recent graduates who have developed practical experience through university or internships.

Understanding User Value

Applicants should be able to recognise what makes a product valuable to users.

Product management is fundamentally concerned with creating products that solve meaningful problems for users while also meeting organisational objectives.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an interest in:

  • User needs.
  • User experience.
  • Product quality.
  • Product improvement.
  • Business outcomes.

Interest in Technology and Product Development

The role requires an interest in:

  • Product development.
  • User experience.
  • Technology.

Applicants do not necessarily need to be software engineers, but they should be comfortable working in a technology-driven environment.

Adaptability

The Disney environment is described as dynamic and fast-paced.

Candidates should be capable of learning quickly and adapting when priorities change.

This is particularly relevant to product management because product priorities can change based on:

  • User feedback.
  • Data.
  • Business priorities.
  • Market conditions.
  • Technical constraints.
  • Competitor activity.

Collaboration

Product management is highly collaborative.

The successful candidate will work across different functions and must be able to build strong professional relationships.

Disney therefore seeks applicants with a collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively in team-oriented environments.

Educational Requirements

The required education is:

An upcoming or recent graduate with a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field.

Relevant related fields may include disciplines closely connected to technology, software, engineering or other technical product-development areas.

Applicants should carefully assess whether their academic programme falls within the “related technical field” requirement.

The vacancy does not state that applicants must have a specific number of years of professional experience. Instead, it specifically accommodates upcoming and recent graduates, with relevant experience potentially coming from coursework, projects and internships.

Learn More HERE

Who Should Consider Applying?

The programme may be relevant to students and recent graduates who want to build careers in:

  • Product management.
  • Technology.
  • Digital products.
  • Software.
  • User experience.
  • Product strategy.
  • Data-informed decision-making.
  • Technology-enabled media.
  • Consumer technology.
  • Digital entertainment.

A candidate might come from a computer science programme, engineering programme or another technical discipline and have developed product-management interests through an internship, university project, student organisation or independent product project.

Salary and Compensation

The listed hiring range for the position in Los Angeles is:

US$97,500 to US$130,700 per year.

The actual base salary offered can vary based on factors including:

  • Internal equity.
  • Geographic region.
  • Job-related knowledge.
  • Skills.
  • Experience.
  • Other relevant considerations.

Disney also states that a bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package.

Additional medical, financial and other benefits may also apply depending on the level and position offered.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between the advertised salary range and the compensation package ultimately offered to an individual candidate.

Location of the Associate Product Manager Program

The job is listed for:

Glendale, California, United States

and

New York, New York, United States.

The posting identifies the Greater Los Angeles, California area as the primary location, while additional opportunities may be available in New York. Final location and team placement will be determined at the time of the offer according to business needs and team alignment.

Candidates should therefore be open to the locations listed in the vacancy.

Start Date

Full-time new hires for the programme will start as a cohort in:

Summer 2027

This means the opportunity is intended for candidates preparing to transition from university into a full-time professional product-management career.

Is There an Application Deadline?

The supplied Disney vacancy does not state a specific application closing date.

The position was posted on September 15, 2026, and applicants should therefore check the official Disney Careers listing regularly because job postings can change or close when recruitment needs are met.

Candidates interested in the programme should not assume that the position will remain open until a particular future date.

Disney’s Approach to Diversity and Inclusion

Disney states that Disney Entertainment & Sports LLC is an equal opportunity employer.

According to the vacancy, applicants are considered without regard to factors including:

  • Race.
  • Religion.
  • Colour.
  • Sex.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Gender identity.
  • Gender expression.
  • National origin.
  • Ancestry.
  • Age.
  • Marital status.
  • Military or veteran status.
  • Medical condition.
  • Genetic information.
  • Disability.
  • Other bases prohibited by applicable law.

The company also states that it welcomes job seekers with disabilities and veterans with disabilities.

This information describes Disney’s stated employment policy; applicants should separately verify any work-authorization or immigration requirements that may apply to employment in the United States.

How to Prepare for the Disney APM Application

Candidates can take several practical steps before applying.

1. Build a Product-Focused Resume

A technical degree alone may not demonstrate product-management potential.

Applicants should highlight projects and experiences that demonstrate:

  • Problem-solving.
  • User research.
  • Product thinking.
  • Data analysis.
  • Technical knowledge.
  • Leadership.
  • Communication.
  • Teamwork.
  • Project execution.

If you have completed a university project that involved identifying a user problem and developing a technology-based solution, explain your role and the outcome clearly.

2. Highlight Relevant Internships

Relevant internships can demonstrate exposure to:

  • Product development.
  • Software.
  • Engineering.
  • UX.
  • Data.
  • Technology.
  • Business strategy.

Applicants should explain what they actually accomplished rather than simply listing the internship title.

3. Demonstrate Data Skills

The APM role involves data analysis.

Candidates should therefore highlight experience with:

  • Data interpretation.
  • Metrics.
  • User behaviour.
  • Analytics.
  • Research.
  • Evidence-based decision-making.

Where appropriate, applicants can describe specific projects in which data influenced a decision.

4. Show User-Centred Thinking

Product managers need to understand users.

Candidates should demonstrate that they can think about:

  • Who the user is.
  • What problem the user faces.
  • Why the problem matters.
  • What solution could address it.
  • How success would be measured.

5. Prepare for Product Management Interviews

Applicants should be prepared to discuss product-related problems and explain how they would approach them.

Useful areas to practise include:

  • Product design.
  • Product strategy.
  • User research.
  • Prioritisation.
  • Metrics.
  • Market analysis.
  • Competitor research.
  • Product launches.
  • Stakeholder management.
  • Communication.

Candidates should be prepared to explain their reasoning rather than simply provide an answer.

How to Demonstrate Product Thinking

A useful way to structure responses to product questions is to begin with the user and the problem.

For example:

  1. Identify the target user.
  2. Define the problem.
  3. Understand why the problem matters.
  4. Identify potential solutions.
  5. Consider technical and business constraints.
  6. Prioritise possible solutions.
  7. Define success metrics.
  8. Consider how the product would be tested.
  9. Measure results.
  10. Improve the product based on evidence.

This type of structured thinking aligns with the responsibilities described in the Disney APM role, including product research, user insights, strategy, roadmaps and data analysis.

Understanding the Disney Product Environment

One distinctive feature of the role is the scale and diversity of the company’s media ecosystem.

Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology supports products and platforms associated with major Disney brands and media properties.

The vacancy describes an environment where technology is used to:

  • Improve storytelling.
  • Build consumer experiences.
  • Support media distribution.
  • Support advertising.
  • Develop digital platforms.
  • Connect audiences with content.
  • Solve complex technical challenges.

For a product-management candidate, this means the work can involve the intersection of technology, business, content and consumer behaviour.

Career Development and Mentorship

The APM programme includes structured training and mentorship from Disney product leaders.

This provides early-career professionals with access to people who have experience managing products and product teams.

The development experience includes learning opportunities focused on:

  • Product management fundamentals.
  • Strategic problem-solving.
  • Leadership.
  • Networking.
  • Product strategy.
  • Data-informed decision-making.

The two-year structure also provides time for participants to develop beyond a short-term internship experience.

Product Management Skills You Can Develop

Through the programme’s responsibilities and training structure, participants can develop skills across several areas.

Product Strategy

Understanding how product objectives connect with broader business goals.

Product Discovery

Learning how to identify user problems and opportunities.

User Research

Using user insights and behaviour to understand product needs.

Data Analysis

Using metrics and behavioural data to inform decisions.

Roadmapping

Helping teams determine which features and initiatives should be developed and when.

Product Requirements

Writing detailed requirements and user stories that help engineering and design teams execute.

Stakeholder Management

Working with product, design, engineering and leadership teams.

Communication

Explaining product strategy and decisions clearly to different audiences.

Launch Management

Supporting the process of taking features from development into launch.

Important Application Considerations

Before applying, candidates should carefully review the official vacancy and consider the following:

  • The position is full-time.
  • The programme begins in Summer 2027.
  • It is structured as a two-year career accelerator.
  • Team rotations occur after 12 months.
  • The primary location is Greater Los Angeles.
  • New York may also be available.
  • Final team and location are determined at the time of offer.
  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field is required.
  • Relevant product, engineering, software or UX experience can come through coursework, projects or internships.
  • The job posting does not provide a fixed application deadline.
  • Salary and additional compensation depend on the final offer and relevant factors.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Disney Associate Product Manager Program 2027.

Key Facts at a Glance

Detail Information

The official Disney listing confirms the programme structure, qualifications, locations, salary range and Summer 2027 start.

How to Apply

Candidates interested in the Disney Associate Product Manager Program should apply through the official Disney Careers application system.

The vacancy is listed under Job ID 10160554.

The application should be prepared around the requirements specified in the job description, particularly:

  • Technical academic background.
  • Product or technical project experience.
  • Analytical ability.
  • Communication.
  • Collaboration.
  • User-centred thinking.
  • Interest in technology.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Adaptability.

Applicants should also review Disney’s candidate resources and hiring-process information before submitting their application.

The official Disney Associate Product Manager Program vacancy provides the current application information.

Conclusion

The Disney Associate Product Manager Program 2027 provides an entry point into product management for upcoming and recent graduates with technical academic backgrounds and an interest in technology, product development and user experience.

The two-year programme combines full-time employment with structured development, mentorship, networking, product-management training and practical experience. Participants will work alongside product managers, designers and engineers, contribute to product strategy, write product requirements, analyse data, conduct competitor research and support product launches.

An important feature of the programme is the 12-month team rotation, which is designed to expose participants to multiple product teams and domains. This gives early-career product professionals an opportunity to broaden their understanding of how product management works across different environments.

The role is based primarily in the Greater Los Angeles area, with potential opportunities in New York City. The listed Los Angeles hiring range is US$97,500 to US$130,700 per year, with possible additional bonus, long-term incentives and benefits depending on the position and final offer.

For applicants, the key academic requirement is an upcoming or recently completed Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field. Candidates can demonstrate relevant experience through coursework, academic projects or internships in product management, engineering, software development, user experience or related areas.

The Disney vacancy does not specify a fixed application deadline, so interested candidates should review the official listing and apply while the position remains open. The role was posted on September 15, 2026, and recruitment listings can change as hiring needs evolve.

For graduates who want to combine technology, data, user needs, business strategy and product development within a major global media organisation, the Disney APM Program offers a structured route into an early product-management career.

Key Summary: 2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship

The 2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme is an opportunity for early-career professionals from members of the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) to gain hands-on training and experience in law, policy and science, while building capacity to support their governments in international processes.

  • Location: New York, USA
  • Fellowship Start: February 2027
  • Duration: One year
  • Monthly Stipend: $5,000 USD per month
  • Settling-in Allowance: $5,000
  • Airfare: Roundtrip economy airfare to New York City
  • Laptop: Provided
  • Health Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance
  • Travel: Travel budget for major international meetings
  • Who Can Apply? Eligible Countries: The 2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme is open to eligible nationals of AOSIS member countries, subject to the programme’s other eligibility requirements. AOSIS includes countries across the Caribbean, Pacific, Atlantic, Indian Ocean and South China Sea regions.
  • Focus Areas: Climate change, ocean, environmental protection and sustainable development
  • Application Deadline: Friday, November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST

Important: Applications must be submitted by the applicant’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York. Individuals interested in applying are advised to contact their Permanent Mission.

2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Application

All applications must be submitted by the Permanent Mission to the United Nations of the Applicant’s country of nationality. Individuals are advised to contact their Permanent Mission if they are interested in applying. Contact information for Permanent Missions can be found at: bluebook.e-delegate.un.org

The Application Deadline is Friday, November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Please review the Fellowship Candidate Requirements in this package or at www.aosis.org/fellowship before applying.

To apply, Permanent Missions should send the Applicant’s completed application form to fellowship@aosis.org, along with the following materials:

Required Application Materials

Note Verbale from the Permanent Mission:
Endorsing the applicant, confirming their inclusion in national delegations for international meetings (including UNFCCC negotiations), guaranteeing and as appropriate committing to seek their post-fellowship government employment, and confirming the Mission’s agreement to fulfill its responsibilities, as outlined in the Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Agreement.

A Written Sample (no longer than 3 pages), addressing the following questions:

  • What unique background, experience, or expertise will you bring to the Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme?
  • What work do you hope to pursue following the Fellowship to continue to support your government’s engagement on climate change, environmental protection, sustainable development, and ocean matters?

Please note: All submissions will be screened for the use of artificial intelligence. The detection of AI-generated content may result in the disqualification of your application.

Passport Biodata Page:
Provide a clear copy of the applicant’s biodata page from a passport that is valid and will not expire within 18 months of the 2027 Fellowship’s start date.

Standardized Curriculum Vitae (no longer than 1 page):
Must explicitly detail your Personal Information (DOB, Age, Gender, Language fluency), Education (Full Degree name(s), University name(s), Month/Year degree attained), and Government/Intergovernmental Experience (Job titles, Entities, Month/Year start and end). Relevant experiences and achievements are welcome.

Important Application Notes

  • All submissions must be in English.
  • Following the submission of a complete application, candidates will be individually contacted to arrange a recorded video interview.
  • Only eligible applications submitted by the Applicant’s Permanent Mission in New York, and with all the above materials included, will be considered for the Fellowship Programme.
  • The Fellowship Programme will begin in New York in February 2027.

Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme

Designed to meet the specific needs of SIDS, the Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme is a unique opportunity for early-career professionals from members of the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) to get hands-on training and experience on issues of law, policy, and science, and to build enduring capacity in AOSIS member governments to engage in international processes.

During the yearlong Fellowship Programme, Fellows will work at their UN Permanent Mission in New York, receive comprehensive training on climate change, ocean, environmental protection, and sustainable development issues, and gain real-world negotiation experience working with their national delegations and AOSIS at related UN conferences.

At the conclusion of the Programme, Fellows will return to their home country having developed the skills and knowledge needed to continue to engage on these issues and in the international process—as many former fellows have continued to do.

What Fellows Can Expect

Fellows can expect:

  • Training on relevant issues of law, policy, and science to build fundamental knowledge and understanding of climate change, environmental protection, sustainable development, and ocean issues;
  • Media training to learn the skills necessary to communicate information to a broader international audience;
  • Real-world negotiation experience at the United Nations to bring back to governments in their countries of origin; and
  • Opportunities to participate in important international conferences.

“The Fellowship was an excellent opportunity. We gained valuable knowledge in key areas that affect SIDS, but we also got hands on experience on how this knowledge is applied in a real-life setting to reach the outcomes SIDS need.”
— Former AOSIS Fellow

Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Terms and Benefits

Fellows agree to:

  • Work full-time in the AOSIS Fellowship Programme under the direction of the AOSIS Fellowship Director and their Mission;
  • Report to the AOSIS Fellowship Director for instructions and assignments on AOSIS priorities;
  • Attend all Fellowship meetings and trainings in New York; and
  • Attend and actively participate in international meetings, including covering priority areas for AOSIS as assigned by the AOSIS Fellowship Directors.

What Fellows Will Receive

  • A roundtrip economy airfare ticket to New York City;
  • A fixed settling-in allowance of $5,000;
  • A laptop computer for use while an AOSIS Fellow;
  • A monthly stipend of $5,000 USD per month (housing costs are to be covered by the stipend);
  • Comprehensive health insurance; and
  • A travel budget to cover the costs of attending major international meetings.

2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Eligibility Requirements

The candidate must:

  • Be a national of an AOSIS country;
  • Be 25 to 32 years old at the beginning of the Fellowship Programme;
  • Hold a degree in a relevant field (international relations, international law, environment, climate change, sustainable development, fisheries, ocean affairs, finance, etc.);
  • Have 1 to 3 years of experience (maximum 5 years) working in a national government, or a regional or international organization;
  • Commit to work in their national government following the completion of the Fellowship;
  • Demonstrate discretion and sound judgement in dealing with politically sensitive issues in a diplomatic environment;
  • Demonstrate excellent academic record and writing skills; and
  • Be proficient in written and spoken English.

Sponsoring Mission Requirements

Sponsoring Missions will:

  • Nominate one Fellow from amongst their nationals through their UN Permanent Mission;
  • Make best efforts to have a position within the government for the Fellow at the end of the Fellowship;
  • Accredit the Fellow to their Mission and to their National delegations attending UNFCCC, BBNJ and other negotiations in which AOSIS participates;
  • Secure a US G-1 visa for the Fellow; and
  • Provide a suitable work, workspace and supervision in their respective Permanent Mission in New York.

How to Apply for the 2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship

Applicants interested in the 2027 Italy-AOSIS Fellowship Programme should contact the Permanent Mission to the United Nations of their country of nationality.

The application must be submitted by the applicant’s Permanent Mission in New York. The Mission should submit the completed application form together with the required Note Verbale, written sample, passport biodata page and standardized CV to fellowship@aosis.org.

📅 Application Deadline

Friday, November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST

item.content:encoded:
The FCDO Research Advisory Group (RAG) is seeking experienced experts to join its advisory group and provide independent scientific and research advice to the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO).

This is a senior-level, part-time advisory opportunity for individuals with substantial expertise in areas such as health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, economic growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development, data for development, big data and artificial intelligence.

Members will contribute strategic advice on FCDO’s research priorities, funding portfolio, evidence use, research quality, value for money, emerging global challenges and connections with the wider UK and international research community.

The position is remote, part-time and unremunerated, although FCDO will reimburse reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses associated with the role.

About the FCDO Research Advisory Group

The FCDO Research Advisory Group was established in 2022 to provide strategic guidance, rapid insight and independent challenge to FCDO’s research funding portfolio.

The Group supports the work of the FCDO Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA), who is also the Director of the Research and Evidence Division.

Its role is to help assure the quality, relevance and appropriateness of FCDO’s research portfolio.

The Group brings together experts with thematic and geographic knowledge covering a wide range of global development and international policy issues.

Its areas of expertise include:

  • Health
  • Agriculture
  • Climate
  • Energy
  • Water
  • Economic growth
  • Humanitarian affairs
  • Education
  • Governance
  • Conflict
  • Social development
  • Data for development
  • Big data
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Innovation and related research areas

Members are expected to contribute their expertise while also engaging with issues that extend beyond their own individual academic discipline.

What Is the Role of an FCDO Research Advisory Group Member?

Members provide independent scientific and research advice to FCDO.

The role is not simply about advising on an individual’s specialist field. Members are appointed in a personal capacity, meaning they serve as independent experts rather than representatives of their employer, profession, institution or an interest group.

Members are also expected to contribute across the Group’s broader agenda.

Their responsibilities include providing insight into how research and evidence can support international development and wider foreign policy objectives.

Key Responsibilities

1. Advising on FCDO Research Priorities

Members will contribute to discussions concerning:

  • FCDO’s research priorities
  • Research activities
  • The relationship between FCDO research and the wider UK science base
  • Connections with international research communities
  • Emerging areas where additional research may be required

Their advice can help FCDO consider whether its research portfolio is addressing important global challenges and research needs.

2. Supporting Evidence-Informed Policy

A central responsibility of the Group is helping ensure that FCDO policy is informed by the best available research and evidence.

Members may therefore be asked to consider the quality, relevance and usefulness of research being used to inform policy.

This requires an understanding of how research can be translated into practical policy and development impact.

3. Reviewing Research Programme Effectiveness

Members will comment on the:

  • Effectiveness of research programmes
  • Value for money of research investments
  • Funding mechanisms for research and development
  • Performance and relevance of research activities

This means applicants should be able to engage with questions concerning not only academic quality but also the practical impact and effectiveness of research funding.

4. Advising on the Research Portfolio

Members will help assess the overall balance and adequacy of FCDO’s research portfolio.

This includes identifying:

  • Research gaps
  • Areas requiring greater attention
  • Areas that may deserve less emphasis
  • Emerging research priorities
  • Opportunities for strengthening the overall portfolio

Members therefore need to be able to think beyond individual research projects and consider research strategically at portfolio level.

5. Horizon-Scanning and Scenario Planning

The Group also participates in horizon-scanning and long-range scenario planning.

This involves considering emerging global challenges and developments that could have implications for research, international development and policy.

Experts should therefore be comfortable thinking about future trends and possible challenges rather than focusing exclusively on current issues.

6. Connecting FCDO With Specialist Expertise

Members can provide advice and connections to specialist expertise across:

  • The UK research community
  • International research institutions
  • Academic networks
  • Relevant specialist fields
  • Global research communities

Their networks and understanding of the international research environment can therefore contribute to the Group’s advisory role.

7. Emergency Response and Disaster Preparedness

Where required, members may also provide advice on scientific inputs to FCDO’s emergency response and disaster preparedness.

This responsibility highlights the importance of having experts who can apply research and evidence to rapidly changing international situations.

Time Commitment

The position is designed to be compatible with other professional responsibilities.

Members are expected to participate in:

  • Four meetings per year
  • Approximately 2.5 to 3 hours per meeting
  • Approximately 2 to 3 hours of reading and preparation for each meeting
  • Occasional additional meetings or direct engagement when FCDO requires specific expert advice

Meeting papers are expected to be circulated approximately one week before each meeting, allowing members time to review the material and prepare.

Meeting dates will be confirmed as far in advance as possible.

There may also be occasional ad hoc requests for expert input between scheduled meetings.

Length of Appointment

The appointment is for:

Three years

The term is renewable once, with a maximum of:

Two terms

This means a member may potentially serve for up to six years if their appointment is renewed.

Remuneration and Expenses

The position is unremunerated.

Members do not receive a salary for serving on the Research Advisory Group.

However, the information provided states that reasonable travel expenses and incidental expenses will be reimbursed by FCDO.

Where travel is required, the stated provision is for economy travel.

Applicants should therefore understand that this is a professional advisory appointment rather than a salaried part-time employment position.

Employment Arrangement

The position is listed as:

Employment Type: Part Time

Location: Remote

The remote nature of the role means that members can participate without being based at a particular FCDO office.

However, applicants should take into account that the role may involve meetings or activities requiring travel, with reasonable eligible travel and incidental expenses reimbursed according to the stated arrangements.

Who Is FCDO Looking For?

The Research Advisory Group is seeking individuals with a combination of subject-matter expertise, senior professional experience, international perspective and the ability to provide independent advice.

The selection criteria emphasize several important characteristics.

Selection Criteria

1. Relevant Thematic Expertise

Applicants should have expertise, skills and experience in a relevant thematic area.

The identified thematic areas include:

  • Health
  • Agriculture
  • Climate
  • Energy
  • Water
  • Growth
  • Humanitarian affairs
  • Education
  • Governance
  • Conflict
  • Social development
  • Data for development

Applicants whose expertise relates to broader research, innovation, technology or evidence issues may also be relevant where their expertise connects with the Group’s agenda.

2. Seniority and International Reputation

The Group is looking for individuals with an appropriate level of seniority and international reputation.

This is therefore a senior expert/advisory appointment rather than an entry-level opportunity.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate a substantial record of expertise and contribution in their relevant field.

3. Familiarity With Government Processes

Applicants should have familiarity with:

  • Government processes
  • Key government policies
  • Policy development
  • The relationship between research and government decision-making

Experience of working with government, public institutions or policy environments can therefore be relevant to the role.

4. Independence and Fairness

Members must be committed to a fair and independent process.

Because the Group provides independent advice, members are expected to approach issues objectively and contribute professional judgement without allowing personal or institutional interests to determine their advice.

5. Breadth of Academic Discipline

The selection process values breadth across academic disciplines.

Applicants should have an understanding of transdisciplinary approaches to global challenges.

This is important because many of the issues addressed by FCDO cannot be examined through one discipline alone.

For example, challenges involving climate, health, development, conflict or technology can involve multiple scientific, social, economic and policy perspectives.

6. International and Global Perspective

Applicants should have an international and global perspective.

Particular emphasis is placed on:

  • Capacity strengthening in the Global South
  • Translation of research into impact
  • Research partnerships
  • Working with international partners
  • Understanding how research can contribute to development outcomes

Experience working across countries, regions or international research networks may therefore be relevant.

FCDO Research and Development Context

The Research Advisory Group operates within a broader FCDO research and development environment.

Following publication of the Global Research and Technology Development (GRTD) Approach Paper, launch of the GRTD website and confirmation of long-term funding, FCDO’s research and development portfolio now includes:

  • A large Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme
  • A smaller but growing non-ODA portfolio

The non-ODA component is focused on broader foreign policy and national security objectives.

This means the Group’s work extends across a diverse research portfolio involving development, international policy and other strategic priorities.

Appointment in a Personal Capacity

A significant condition of the appointment is that members serve in their personal capacity.

They are not appointed as representatives of:

  • Their employer
  • Their university
  • Their profession
  • An interest group
  • Another organization

Members are also expected to contribute across the full agenda of the Research Advisory Group, rather than restricting their contribution exclusively to their own academic discipline.

This makes breadth of perspective and the ability to engage with multidisciplinary issues particularly important.

Principles and Standards Expected of Members

Members must abide by the Seven Principles of Public Life, commonly known as the Nolan Principles.

They are also expected to take account of the Government Chief Scientific Adviser (GCSA)’s Principles of Scientific Advice to Government.

These expectations reinforce the importance of:

  • Independence
  • Integrity
  • Evidence
  • Professional conduct
  • Responsible advisory practice
  • Transparency around interests

Declaration of Interests

Successful members must complete a declaration of interests when appointed.

The declaration must also be kept up to date throughout their appointment.

This is important because members may be involved in discussions concerning research programmes, funding mechanisms and research priorities.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to disclose relevant interests and maintain accurate declarations during their term.

Confidentiality and Information Security

Members will have responsibilities concerning FCDO information and documentation.

FCDO documents and information used by the Group are Official UK Government papers and must not be shared outside the Group.

Members will therefore be responsible for safeguarding:

  • FCDO documents
  • Research-related information
  • Meeting papers
  • Advisory materials
  • Other official information provided to the Group

Applicants should be comfortable working within appropriate confidentiality and information-security requirements.

Selection Process

The selection process involves several stages.

Step 1: Submit an Application

Interested applicants are required to submit:

  • A CV
  • An expression of interest

The application should demonstrate how the applicant’s experience, expertise and perspective correspond to the requirements of the Research Advisory Group.

Step 2: Shortlisting

Applications will be reviewed and suitable candidates will be shortlisted.

The selection criteria include thematic expertise, seniority, international reputation, government familiarity, independence, multidisciplinary perspective and international experience.

Step 3: Panel Interview

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a panel interview.

The panel will be led by the Co-Chairs and will include the:

  • Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA), and/or
  • Deputy Chief Scientific Adviser (Deputy CSA)

Candidates should therefore be prepared to discuss their expertise, experience, understanding of research-policy relationships and ability to contribute to the Group’s broader agenda.

Application Deadline

The stated application deadline is:

30 September at 11:59 PM UK time

Important Application Form Instruction

Because this is a part-time and unremunerated position, applicants are specifically instructed to enter:

N/A

in both the:

  • Salary expectations field
  • Notice period field

Applicants should follow this instruction rather than entering a salary expectation or employment notice period.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in joining the FCDO Research Advisory Group should prepare a strong CV and expression of interest addressing their suitability for the position.

The application should demonstrate relevant evidence of:

  1. Thematic expertise
  2. Senior professional experience
  3. International experience or perspective
  4. Understanding of government and policy processes
  5. Independent and fair judgement
  6. Multidisciplinary or transdisciplinary experience
  7. Research translation and impact
  8. Capacity strengthening, particularly in the Global South
  9. Relevant professional and academic networks
  10. Ability to contribute to the Group beyond a narrow disciplinary area

Applicants should also ensure that the salary expectations and notice period fields contain N/A, as instructed in the vacancy announcement.

Apply Here

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity Member, FCDO Research Advisory Group
Organization Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)
Role Type Part-time advisory appointment
Location Remote
Appointment Length 3 years
Renewal Renewable once
Maximum Terms 2 terms
Meetings 4 per year
Meeting Duration 2.5–3 hours
Preparation 2–3 hours per meeting
Additional Commitment Occasional ad hoc input
Remuneration Unremunerated
Travel Reasonable economy travel reimbursed
Incidental Expenses Reimbursed by FCDO
Main Focus Research, evidence, science advice and research funding
Key Expertise Health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development and data for development
Application CV and expression of interest
Selection Shortlisting followed by panel interview
Interview Panel Co-Chairs and CSA and/or Deputy CSA
Deadline 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time
Salary Expectations Field Enter N/A
Notice Period Field Enter N/A

Important Considerations Before Applying

Potential applicants should consider the following before submitting an application:

1. It is a senior-level position

The selection criteria specifically mention seniority and international reputation.

2. It is unpaid

The role is unremunerated, although reasonable travel and incidental expenses are reimbursed.

3. It requires ongoing commitment

There are four meetings each year, preparation for each meeting and occasional additional requests for advice.

4. Independence is important

Members serve in their personal capacity and must support a fair and independent process.

5. Confidentiality is required

Members will have responsibilities for safeguarding Official UK Government documents and information.

6. Multidisciplinary thinking is expected

Members are expected to contribute across the Group’s agenda rather than only discussing their own specialist area.

7. International experience is relevant

The selection criteria specifically refer to an international and global perspective and capacity strengthening in the Global South.

Read Full Details about this Job opportunity HERE

Conclusion

The Member, FCDO Research Advisory Group opportunity provides experienced research and policy experts with the opportunity to contribute independent scientific and research advice to the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.

The Group plays a strategic role in examining FCDO’s research priorities, assessing research programmes and funding mechanisms, identifying gaps, considering emerging global challenges and strengthening the connection between research evidence and policy.

The position is particularly relevant to senior experts with substantial thematic expertise, international perspective, familiarity with government processes, multidisciplinary experience and a strong understanding of how research can be translated into policy and practical impact.

Members will serve for an initial three-year term, renewable once, and will participate in four meetings each year alongside occasional additional advisory activities. The position is remote and part-time but is unremunerated, with reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses reimbursed by FCDO.

Applicants should submit a CV and expression of interest and be prepared for a panel interview if shortlisted. The stated deadline is 30 September at 11:59 PM UK time. Applicants should also enter N/A in the salary expectations and notice period fields because the position is part-time and unremunerated.

item.content:encoded:
Are you an undergraduate student interested in investment management, private credit, private equity, financial analysis, valuation, and private-market investing? Morgan Stanley is offering a 10-week 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program – Private Credit & Equity in New York, United States.

The program is designed for undergraduate students who want to gain practical exposure to the investment management industry and develop skills that are relevant to careers in private markets and investment analysis.

Participants will join Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s Tactical Value team, where they will work alongside investment professionals on research, financial analysis, investment opportunities, portfolio monitoring, and other activities connected to the investment decision-making process.

The application deadline is September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM Eastern Time (ET), while applicants must complete their HireVue digital questionnaire by September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET.

About Morgan Stanley Investment Management

Morgan Stanley Investment Management (MSIM), together with its investment advisory affiliates, operates as part of Morgan Stanley’s global investment management platform. According to the opportunity description, MSIM has more than 1,300 investment professionals worldwide and $2 trillion in assets under management or supervision as of June 30, 2026.

Morgan Stanley describes its investment management business as focused on providing long-term investment performance, client service, and investment management solutions to a diverse range of clients, including governments, institutions, corporations, and individual investors.

Morgan Stanley also maintains a dedicated careers platform for students, graduates, and experienced professionals, with opportunities across investment banking, investment management, wealth management, technology, and other areas.

Opportunity Overview

The 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program – Private Credit & Equity is a 10-week summer internship beginning in June 2027.

The program combines formal training with practical experience inside a specific Investment Management team.

The structure includes:

  1. One week of training
  2. Nine weeks working within the assigned Investment Management team

During the program, Summer Analysts are expected to gain exposure to the professional environment of Morgan Stanley and perform work that is similar in nature to the responsibilities of a full-time Analyst.

The program is designed as a learning and development opportunity. Morgan Stanley specifically notes that participation in this role does not necessarily correlate with full-time opportunities within the firm.

Program Location

Location: New York, United States

The position is based within Morgan Stanley’s Investment Management business in New York.

Morgan Stanley maintains a global presence and states that its employees work across 41 countries, with opportunities available to students and graduates in different regions.

Team: Tactical Value

Successful participants will join the Tactical Value team.

The Tactical Value team focuses on identifying and evaluating opportunistic investment opportunities across private markets.

This provides Summer Analysts with an opportunity to learn about how investment professionals examine potential investments, conduct research, assess companies and industries, evaluate financial information, and contribute to the investment process.

Participants can expect exposure to areas including:

  • Private-market investing
  • Private credit
  • Private equity
  • Investment research
  • Financial analysis
  • Company analysis
  • Industry research
  • Financial forecasting
  • Valuation
  • Portfolio analysis
  • Investment due diligence
  • Investment memoranda
  • Market developments
  • Portfolio-company monitoring
  • Project management

This combination of research, quantitative analysis, qualitative assessment, and investment-related work can provide students with a practical introduction to the processes used in private-market investing.

What Will Summer Analysts Do?

The internship involves a range of investment-related responsibilities.

1. Conduct Investment Due Diligence

Summer Analysts will work with senior members of the Fund to conduct due diligence on potential investment opportunities.

Due diligence involves gathering and analyzing information about a prospective investment so that investment professionals can better understand its financial position, business model, industry, risks, opportunities, and overall investment characteristics.

Students may therefore have opportunities to develop their ability to:

  • Research companies
  • Examine financial information
  • Investigate industries and markets
  • Identify important investment considerations
  • Organize information for senior investment professionals
  • Support the evaluation of prospective investments

2. Coordinate With Advisors and Consultants

Participants may also coordinate with external advisors and consultants involved in investment due diligence.

This responsibility can expose interns to the collaborative nature of investment transactions, where investment teams may work with professionals from different areas to obtain specialized information and analysis.

Strong communication, organization, attention to detail, and professionalism are therefore important.

3. Build Financial Forecasts and Valuation Models

One of the more analytical components of the internship involves helping construct company financial forecasts and valuation models.

This can involve working with financial information to understand a company’s historical performance and develop assumptions about potential future performance.

Students interested in investment management can gain practical experience in areas such as:

  • Financial forecasting
  • Revenue and expense analysis
  • Financial statement analysis
  • Valuation
  • Investment assumptions
  • Financial modeling
  • Quantitative analysis

These are important skills for professionals working in investment management and private markets.

4. Support Other Investment-Related Activities

Summer Analysts may also assist with other investment-related activities.

The opportunity description specifically mentions tasks such as:

  • Tracking prospective investment deals
  • Assisting with confidentiality agreements
  • Supporting investment-related projects
  • Organizing information associated with potential investments
  • Helping investment professionals with ongoing analysis

This means the internship is not limited to financial modeling. Participants may be exposed to the broader workflow involved in evaluating and progressing investment opportunities.

5. Contribute to Investment Memoranda

Participants will also have the opportunity to contribute to investment memoranda relating to investment opportunities.

An investment memorandum typically brings together relevant research and analysis so that investment professionals can evaluate a potential transaction or investment opportunity.

This responsibility can help students develop their ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally.

Skills that may be developed include:

  • Written communication
  • Investment research
  • Data interpretation
  • Company analysis
  • Industry analysis
  • Presentation of findings
  • Attention to detail
  • Business writing

6. Monitor Existing Portfolio Companies

The role also involves monitoring the performance of existing portfolio companies.

This can help interns understand that investment management does not end when an investment is made. Investment professionals may continue to monitor companies, markets, financial performance, and other factors affecting their investments.

Participants can therefore gain insight into portfolio management and ongoing investment analysis.

7. Follow Financial and Economic Developments

Summer Analysts will also be expected to keep current with market developments.

This includes following developments such as:

  • Changes in the economy
  • Financial-market movements
  • New investment products
  • Developments affecting private markets
  • Broader market trends

Developing this habit can help students understand how economic and market developments can affect investment decisions.

Skills You Can Develop Through the Program

The internship is designed to help participants develop a broad set of professional and technical skills.

Financial and Investment Skills

Participants can gain exposure to:

  • Financial modeling
  • Company valuation
  • Investment research
  • Due diligence
  • Portfolio analysis
  • Private-market investing
  • Financial forecasting
  • Investment evaluation

Research and Analytical Skills

The role can also strengthen:

  • Quantitative analysis
  • Qualitative company research
  • Industry research
  • Problem-solving
  • Critical thinking
  • Attention to detail
  • Economic and market analysis

Communication Skills

Because participants will work with investment professionals and potentially interact with advisors and consultants, communication is an important component of the role.

The program specifically highlights opportunities to develop:

  • Public speaking
  • Written communication
  • Presentation skills
  • Professional communication
  • Company and industry analysis

Project Management

Participants will also have opportunities to develop project-management skills, including the ability to:

  • Manage competing priorities
  • Organize research
  • Track prospective deals
  • Meet deadlines
  • Work independently
  • Collaborate with colleagues
  • Present information effectively

Who Should Apply?

The program is particularly relevant to undergraduate students who are interested in careers involving:

  • Investment management
  • Private equity
  • Private credit
  • Asset management
  • Financial analysis
  • Investment banking
  • Corporate finance
  • Valuation
  • Private markets
  • Portfolio management
  • Financial research

Applicants should have a genuine interest in investing and be prepared to demonstrate analytical ability, academic achievement, communication skills, teamwork, and motivation.

You do not necessarily need to have already worked in private equity or private credit. The program itself is structured as a learning and development experience for students.

Key Candidate Qualities

Morgan Stanley is looking for candidates who demonstrate several professional qualities.

Exceptional Academic Performance

Applicants should demonstrate strong academic performance.

Academic achievement can be particularly relevant for competitive investment-management internships because students are expected to analyze complex information and learn technical concepts quickly.

Strong Communication Skills

Candidates should have strong verbal and written communication skills.

This is important because the role involves research, presentations, investment memoranda, collaboration, and communication with other professionals.

Teamwork

Applicants should be comfortable working as part of a team.

Investment management involves collaboration between investment professionals, analysts, advisors, consultants, and other stakeholders.

Independence and Initiative

Morgan Stanley is also looking for self-starters who can work independently.

Candidates should be able to take responsibility for assigned work, organize their tasks, identify information they need, and make progress without requiring constant supervision.

Motivation and Results Orientation

Applicants should demonstrate that they are driven, highly motivated, and focused on producing quality results.

Organization and Time Management

Because Summer Analysts may work on multiple projects and competing priorities, strong organizational and time-management skills are important.

Problem-Solving Ability

The role requires an analytical and detail-oriented mindset.

Candidates should be able to examine information, identify important issues, and contribute to solving investment-related problems.

Interest in Investing

A clear interest in investing is specifically listed as a job requirement.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate why they are interested in investment management and, particularly, private-market investing.

Program Structure

The program will run for approximately 10 weeks beginning in June 2027.

The structure is:

Week 1 — Training

Participants begin with formal training intended to provide foundational knowledge and skills needed for the Investment Management environment.

Weeks 2–10 — Team Placement

The remaining nine weeks involve working within a specific Investment Management team.

For this opportunity, participants will join the Tactical Value team and gain hands-on exposure to research, financial analysis, investment-related projects, and the investment decision-making process.

Compensation

The stated expected base pay rate is:

$36.06 per hour

at the commencement of employment.

Morgan Stanley notes that base pay is determined on an individualized basis and forms only part of the overall compensation package.

Depending on the position, compensation may also include other forms of compensation and benefits, such as:

  • Incentive compensation
  • Discretionary bonuses
  • Commission earnings where applicable
  • Other short- and long-term incentive packages
  • Morgan Stanley-sponsored benefit programs

The exact compensation package should be confirmed through the official employment documentation and applicable terms for the position.

Application Process

Candidates must complete the application process through Morgan Stanley.

The stated process requires applicants to:

Step 1: Submit Your Resume

Candidates must submit their resume through the Morgan Stanley careers website.

Morgan Stanley maintains an online careers platform specifically for students, graduates, and experienced professionals.

Step 2: Complete the HireVue Questionnaire

Applicants must also complete the required HireVue digital questionnaire.

Completing the questionnaire by the specified deadline is necessary for the application to be considered.

Step 3: Submit Before the Deadline

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, meaning candidates are encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the final day.

The position may close when it is filled or when the stated application deadline is reached.

Important Application Deadlines

Applicants should pay attention to two separate deadlines.

Application Deadline

September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET

This is the deadline stated for submitting the application.

HireVue Deadline

September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET

Applicants must complete their HireVue responses by this deadline.

Because the application is reviewed on a rolling basis, students interested in the opportunity should consider submitting their application as early as possible.

What Should Applicants Highlight in Their Resume?

Students applying for this opportunity should make sure their resume clearly demonstrates the skills Morgan Stanley identifies in the job description.

Relevant areas to highlight include:

  • Strong academic performance
  • Financial or investment-related coursework
  • Finance clubs or investment societies
  • Business or economics projects
  • Financial modeling experience
  • Excel proficiency
  • Data analysis
  • Research experience
  • Leadership experience
  • Teamwork
  • Public speaking
  • Presentation experience
  • Project management
  • Entrepreneurial activities
  • Relevant internships
  • Investment-related personal projects

Applicants who do not have formal investment experience can still demonstrate relevant skills through academic projects, student organizations, research, competitions, leadership activities, or other analytical experiences.

What Makes the Tactical Value Team Relevant to Private Markets?

The Tactical Value team focuses on opportunistic investment opportunities across private markets.

Private-market investing differs from publicly traded-market investing because investment opportunities can involve privately held companies, private credit arrangements, and other investments that are not necessarily traded on public stock exchanges.

Working within this environment can expose students to the process of identifying potential opportunities, researching companies, analyzing financial information, assessing valuations, conducting due diligence, and monitoring investments.

The experience described in the position therefore combines several areas of investment work rather than focusing exclusively on one technical function.

Why This Internship Can Be Valuable for Students Interested in Finance

The program provides exposure to several fundamental areas of investment management within a major global financial-services organization.

Rather than being limited to classroom learning, participants are expected to work on actual research and investment-related activities, including financial forecasting, valuation, due diligence, investment memoranda, portfolio monitoring, and market research.

The program can therefore help students understand how investment professionals evaluate opportunities and make decisions based on financial, company, industry, and market information.

Morgan Stanley also states that its student and graduate opportunities are intended to provide opportunities for talented students and recent graduates to develop their careers within the firm.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, candidates should keep the following points in mind:

  1. The position is a summer internship, not a permanent job.
  2. It is based in New York.
  3. Applicants must be pursuing a Bachelor’s degree.
  4. Applicants must graduate between December 2028 and June 2029.
  5. The program lasts 10 weeks.
  6. The program begins with one week of training.
  7. The remaining nine weeks involve team-based work.
  8. Participants will join the Tactical Value team.
  9. The role focuses heavily on private-market investment activities.
  10. Strong analytical, communication, organizational, and teamwork skills are expected.
  11. Applicants should demonstrate a keen interest in investing.
  12. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
  13. The application deadline is September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET.
  14. HireVue responses must be completed by September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET.
  15. The stated expected base pay is $36.06 per hour at the commencement of employment.
  16. Participation in the internship does not guarantee or necessarily correspond to a full-time position at Morgan Stanley.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should apply through Morgan Stanley’s official careers platform and complete the required application and HireVue process.

Apply HERE

Conclusion

The Morgan Stanley 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program – Private Credit & Equity is a 10-week undergraduate summer internship based in New York that provides exposure to private-market investing and the investment management process.

Participants will join the Tactical Value team and have opportunities to contribute to investment research, due diligence, financial forecasting, valuation modeling, investment memoranda, portfolio monitoring, market analysis, and other investment-related projects.

The program is designed for Bachelor’s degree students graduating between December 2028 and June 2029, with Morgan Stanley seeking candidates who demonstrate strong academic performance, communication ability, analytical thinking, teamwork, initiative, organization, problem-solving skills, and a genuine interest in investing.

With an expected base pay rate of $36.06 per hour, a structured 10-week program, formal training, and practical exposure to private-market investment activities, the opportunity provides undergraduate students with a direct introduction to investment management.

Interested applicants should note the two critical deadlines: September 25, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET for the application and September 27, 2026, at 11:55 PM ET for the HireVue questionnaire. Since applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, eligible students should prepare their resumes and application materials well before the deadline.
